description:
We are a group of Georgian engineers. While still students, our skills are broad. From circuit design to SMD soldering, from reverse engineering stubborn products to simulating antennas and electric fields, from software development, low-level or high, to experience design and games.

Point is, we are here to make things tick or break things and try ourselves under pressure.

May the best be victorious,
May the Force be with you,

Regards, the Mango Force team!
summary: SPEARv is a public web tool for NASA SPHEREx sky images. You enter Right Ascension and Declination, pick a field of view and data release, hit Find, and get that patch as multi-epoch images you can blink like a little video to spot movers. It is written in Rust, Axum, and React, with Utoipa for the OpenAPI spec, and runs on OCI. An index of the public SPHEREx S3 bucket turns exposures into a fast query table that points at the real objects; RA/Dec and FOV drive patch fetches and server-side mosaics. That matches the challenge: coordinates in, change-over-time out, on real survey data, for anyone. SPHEREx maps the whole sky about every six months in 102 near-IR bands with far more objects than one person can sift; SPEARv makes that searchable by eye. Live at https://mango.forces.quest.
details:
It works! We think..

Visit https://mango.forces.quest to check it out!

So. It is written in Rust, Axum, and React, with Utoipa forming our OpenAPI spec. It runs on OCI Cloud due to cheap and fast networking.

It indexes the public SPHEREx S3 bucket into a fast queryable table of exposures with directions and coordinates that references the actual S3 objects. RA and Dec get referenced to that, then according to the FOV requested it fetches data in patches and assembles them as a mosaic. Biggest image we have tried so far is 25 degrees lengthwise and widthwise, pulling about 288 GB of data from the bucket before the compute step.
